block: yx-bootmig P4 is owned by the olamnit lane, but only SHIRAS has all four target repos on disk, so the owning lane can never discharge a P4 era.
background: Ruling Q-ERAOWN-01 (yngenios/specs/008-yx-bootmig-base/spec.md:10) assigns the era to lane olamnit @ OLAMNIT.
SKILL.md precondition 3 refuses because three of four targets are 'lane slugs, not repo roots', making migration into them NOT-DISCHARGEABLE-HERE.
Measured on SHIRAS 2026-09-03 with git rev-parse + git ls-files: yngenios-windows 5149 tracked, yngenios-linux 1010, yngenios-app 1686, yngenios 3418 - ALL FOUR are real git repos here.
The skill's own Honest limits section records SHIRAS as UNMEASURED; M3 was a GAVRIELLA-vantage measurement.
gavriella's SOURCE-HANDOFF 20260902T1845Z is addressed to @yngwin/@ynglin/@yngapp as target owners, and carries ruling Q-YXBOOTMIG-P3-01 (RESYNTHESIS against L0).
impact_if_unanswered: P4 cannot start anywhere: the lane holding the ruling cannot write to three of four targets, and the host that can write to them holds no mandate. The engineer's replicate-olamnit-capability directive stalls indefinitely while appearing merely blocked on P3.

options.label: Split: olamnit rules, SHIRAS discharges
options.consequence: Q-ERAOWN-01 stands for delineation and rulings; SHIRAS is named execution host for P4 eras. Costs a cross-host handoff per era and manifest agreement before each era opens.

options.label: Override Q-ERAOWN-01 to glpnet/shiras
options.consequence: Fastest start, but overrides a recorded ruling, risks duplicating olamnit's in-flight work against Q-MARATHON-02, and requires re-pointing three target lanes.

options.label: Leave with olamnit; file evidence only
options.consequence: Zero duplication risk, but defers rather than resolves; P4 stays blocked until target disks or a handoff exist anyway.

options.label: Re-examine fleet target topology
options.consequence: Treats reachability as the real defect; largest scope and blocks P4 longest.

recommendation.because: It is the only option that preserves the recorded ruling AND removes the physical impossibility; overriding duplicates a peer lane's work and evidence-only leaves the engineer's directive unadvanced.

decision.rationale: Engineer accepted the recommendation: olamnit retains P4 rulings under Q-ERAOWN-01; SHIRAS is the execution host because it is the only measured host holding all four target repos.

block: The GLPNET repo instruction file bans AskUserQuestion outright while the canonical fleet standard BK-STD-2 names AskUserQuestion as the required interactive surface
background: GLPNET CLAUDE.md: 'Never ask closed-form questions (multiple choice, yes/no, pick-from-list, AskUserQuestion). Free-text only when clarification is genuinely needed.'

ANSWER-20260903T1000Z-gavriella-hatzinor, closing a help request asked twice: 'THE INTERACTIVE QUESTION TEMPLATE IS AskUserQuestion, NOT A FILE.' BK-STD-2 is the content standard and the durable record; there is no template file to find on any host.
The template was shaped by ariellas 20260824T0635Z, extended by gavriella, hardened by olamnit 20260824T0800Z - four lanes converged on one shape.
The engineer instructed this lane in-session to present questions interactively using the standard templates.
impact_if_unanswered: Any lane inheriting GLPNET's CLAUDE.md silently fails to present BK-STD-2 questions in canonical form and looks non-compliant while obeying its own repo; the durable record loses cross-host comparability.

options.label: BK-STD-2 wins; amend GLPNET CLAUDE.md
options.consequence: Carve out BK-STD-2 engineer questions from the ban, keeping free-text as the default for ordinary clarification. One-line edit.

options.label: CLAUDE.md wins; free-text only here
options.consequence: Preserves the lane preference but this lane's questions render differently from every other lane's, and it contradicts the engineer's in-session instruction.

options.label: Interactive picker plus free-text follow-up
options.consequence: Highest fidelity to how the engineer refines designs mid-discussion; costs more turns and the local rule still needs amending to be literally true.

recommendation.because: A fleet standard hardened by four lanes beats one repo's local preference, and it is what the engineer just instructed; the carve-out keeps the free-text default intact for everything else.

decision.rationale: Engineer accepted the recommendation: BK-STD-2 carve-out added to GLPNET CLAUDE.md; free-text remains the default for ordinary clarification.

block: S1's three-line phase fix lives in the buildkit repo, a shared checkout this lane does not own, under a do-not-re-fork ruling.
background: All three transition writers omit phase: readiness.py:126-136, onboard.py:285-292, flow/__main__.py:866-870. board_phase_seconds skips a phase-less op by design.
flow/__main__.py:890 does pass phase=implement but to _takt_emit, a different sink, 20 lines later.
Ruling Q-ERASTAGE-03: escalate to the buildkit lane, do not re-fork.
buildkit is a shared checkout across 5+ lanes and was measured sitting on feat/093-fleet-convergence-protocol, not develop.
impact_if_unanswered: Board-side phase intervals stay unmeasurable fleet-wide, so scheduler_ops contributes 0 phases to every takt report and CPM/PERT duration work has no board-side input.

options.label: File to @buildkit with the patch spelled out
options.consequence: Exact files, lines and the sink-mismatch explanation so the owning lane applies a 3-line change with no re-derivation. This lane's era ends at 'filed', not 'fixed'.

options.label: Patch buildkit directly on a branch
options.consequence: Fastest measurable fix but edits an unowned shared checkout against an explicit ruling; it forecloses the clean lane-separation record, because once this lane has written to buildkit the do-not-re-fork ruling can no longer be shown to have held, and it risks sweeping in a concurrent lane's WIP that cannot be un-swept

options.label: Escalate as a roadmap feature
options.consequence: Survives inattention rather than depending on the buildkit lane noticing a COOP message; slower to land.

recommendation.because: It honours Q-ERASTAGE-03 and lane separation while removing all re-derivation cost from the owning lane; patching directly trades a 3-line saving for a shared-checkout collision risk.

decision.rationale: Engineer accepted the recommendation: filed to @buildkit in COOP ACK section 6 with exact files, line numbers and root cause; no cross-lane edit.

block: The shipped yx-bootmig skill file hard-refuses on preconditions measured STALE on this host, so a future SHIRAS session refuses wrongly
background: Precondition 3 claims three targets are absent; all four are present on SHIRAS (5149/1010/1686/3418 tracked).
The root table gives glpnet as D:/BSTDEV/research/GLP/glpnet, which does not exist on SHIRAS; the real root is research/crucible/glp/GLPNET with 8114 tracked.
FR-9 already requires roots resolved from config and verified BY CONTENT, never inherited.
The skill's PROVENANCE says the yngenios spec is the owner and wins any disagreement.
impact_if_unanswered: The next SHIRAS session either refuses wrongly or re-derives the same measurement, which is the rediscovery loop the programme's reporting rules exist to prevent.

options.label: Add measured per-host note, keep refusal logic
options.consequence: Records date, method and host beside precondition 3 and the root table without weakening any refusal; makes the skill obey its own FR-9.

options.label: Correct preconditions and root table outright
options.consequence: Cleanest end state but the upstream yngenios spec must change too or the two diverge again.

options.label: Leave the skill; record in COOP and marathon only
options.consequence: Zero edit risk but guarantees the next session repeats the work.

recommendation.because: It stops the wrong refusal at zero risk to the refusal logic that is correct on other hosts, and it is FR-9 applied to the targets rather than a new rule.

decision.rationale: Engineer accepted the recommendation: per-host measured notes added at precondition 3 and the root table; refusal logic left unchanged.
